body.statement: Uniformly over \(\mathcal M\), \(\|\widehat w_\ell-w_\ell\|_2=O_{\Pr}(n_\ell^{-1/2})\), with curvature supplied by \(v^\top H_\ell v\geq\lambda\|v\|_2^2\) on \(L\) at every \(\ell\). Along every extracted subsequence for which \(H_\ell\to H\) and \(\sqrt{n_\ell}w_{\ell j}\to h_j\in[0,\infty]\), \(\sqrt{n_\ell}(\widehat w_\ell-w_\ell)\Rightarrow V_h\), where only the subsequential limit criterion defining \(V_h\) uses \(H\). Moreover, \(A_t(V_h)=0\) almost surely if and only if all donor post-period quantile functions coincide almost everywhere; a projection face contributes an atom at zero exactly when that face lies in \(\ker M_t\).
body.justification: Finite-array curvature identifies the weight uniformly, while its subsequential limit \(H\) governs the moving tangent-set Gaussian projection when the unique DSC weight approaches a simplex face.
body.gap: Canen and Song give inference for a simplex-valued optimizer and Andrews gives boundary extremum limits; neither transports the projected score through a discrete post-period quantile loss.
body.consumer: It identifies when learned boundary weights contribute first-order uncertainty to each post-period QTE curve relative to the donor-identified no-intervention counterfactual.
